title: Tools
subtitle: Find what can help you right now.

items.currentLoad: What am I carrying right now

savedEmpty: Nothing saved yet. Save a tool and it waits for you here.
recentEmpty: Once you have used a tool, it shows up here.

blurbs.questionnaire: Teaches the coach how you actually work.
blurbs.communication: Sets the voice the app uses when you are struggling.
blurbs.lifeWheel: Eight parts of your life, and which one is quietly costing you.
blurbs.valuesClarity: Which five values you want to live by, and how far you are from them.
blurbs.bestYear: Write from a year ahead, and meet it again when it arrives.
blurbs.direction: One sentence about where you are pointed. Not a goal, and nothing is planned from it.
blurbs.passionMap: What draws you in, tested against real days.
blurbs.mirror: What people who know you see, when you ask them properly.
blurbs.gratitude: Writes down five things worth keeping from the day, and keeps them for you alone.
blurbs.whatWorked: Takes one thing that went well and shows you what helped it happen.
blurbs.selfCompassion: Gives a hard moment one minute of quiet, and asks nothing of you.
blurbs.decisionClarity: Lays out the four sides of a hard decision without deciding for you.
blurbs.currentLoad: Turns a heavy week into something you can actually look at.
blurbs.obstacle: Turns the thing that keeps stopping you into one sentence you can act on.
blurbs.supportMap: Shows who you would want beside you, and in which moments.

lifeWheel.title: Life Wheel

intro.lead: Eight parts of a life, eight minutes.
intro.body: For each one you answer two things: how it is going, and how much it matters to you right now. The second question is the one that makes the first one mean something. Nothing here is scored and nothing is shared.
intro.resume: Pick up where you left off

blurb.health: Your body, your sleep, your energy.
blurb.relationships: The people you choose, and how close they feel.
blurb.family: The people you did not choose.
blurb.career: The work itself, not the job title.
blurb.money: What you have, and how much you have to think about it.
blurb.growth: Learning, and becoming someone slightly different.
blurb.fun: The part of the week that is not useful.
blurb.environment: Where you live, and whether it holds you.

lifeWheel.satisfaction: How is your {{area}} going right now?
lifeWheel.weight: And how much does it matter to you at the moment?

result.title: Your wheel
result.lead: This is the shape of your life right now, in your own numbers.
result.pressingOne: The area costing you most is {{area}}. It matters {{weight}} out of ten and it is at {{satisfaction}}.
result.pressingTwo: Two areas are asking for something: {{first}} and {{second}}. Both matter more than they are currently getting.
result.pressingNone: Nothing on your wheel is far from where you want it. That is worth noticing rather than rushing past.
result.strongest: {{area}} is carrying you at the moment. It is worth knowing what you are doing right there.
result.lowButFine: Some areas are low and do not matter much right now, and that is a life with priorities in it. This tool never treats a low number on its own as a problem.
result.next: Nothing happens automatically from this. If one of these is worth working on, the coach is there when you want it.
result.dreamsLead: Would you like to keep this as a Dream? A Dream is something you are aiming at, not a plan — nothing gets scheduled.
result.dreamAdded: {{area}} is one of your Dreams now.
result.dreamExists: You already have a Dream for {{area}}.

descriptions.authenticity: To live and act in a way that is true to who I am.
descriptions.independence: To make my own decisions and steer my own life.
descriptions.freedom: To keep room to choose how I live and act.
descriptions.choice: To know I can always choose how I respond.
descriptions.creativity: To bring new ideas and expressions into the world.
descriptions.learning: To keep gaining knowledge and skill.
descriptions.growth: To keep developing into who I want to be.
descriptions.openness: To meet ideas, people and experiences unlike my own.
descriptions.adaptability: To adapt to change without losing myself.
descriptions.achievement: To set goals and reach results that mean something.
descriptions.excellence: To do things to a standard I am proud of.
descriptions.perseverance: To keep going when the way gets hard.
descriptions.selfDiscipline: To act on what matters to me even when I do not feel like it.
descriptions.ambition: To reach further and widen what is possible for me.
descriptions.responsibility: To stand behind my choices and my actions.
descriptions.professionalism: To work with skill, seriousness and care.
descriptions.efficiency: To use my time and resources well.
descriptions.impact: To make a real difference to people or to the world.
descriptions.fulfilment: To use what I am capable of and reach something that matters.
descriptions.courage: To act in spite of fear or uncertainty.
descriptions.determination: To stay committed to what matters to me.
descriptions.boldness: To try without being promised it will work.
descriptions.resilience: To recover from difficulty and carry on.
descriptions.adjusting: To find another way when reality changes.
descriptions.risk: To leave my comfort zone for something worth it.
descriptions.patience: To give processes and people the time they need.
descriptions.selfAcceptance: To accept myself while I am still becoming.
descriptions.selfCompassion: To treat myself as a human being in hard moments.
descriptions.hope: To believe a better future can be built.
descriptions.stability: To feel secure, ordered and continuous.
descriptions.health: To look after my body and my mind.
descriptions.balance: To give the different parts of my life their place.
descriptions.love: To give and receive warmth, care and closeness.
descriptions.family: To invest in the bonds and the duties of family.
descriptions.familyLife: To keep the relationships inside my family alive.
descriptions.friendship: To build close relationships built on being there.
descriptions.intimacy: To allow closeness, vulnerability and being known.
descriptions.belonging: To feel part of a group or a relationship.
descriptions.trust: To build bonds where it is safe to rely on each other.
descriptions.loyalty: To stay beside the people and the principles that matter.
descriptions.partnership: To build and act together, responsible to each other.
descriptions.listening: To give somebody else's experience real room.
descriptions.respect: To treat myself and others as worth something.
descriptions.kindness: To meet others with gentleness and generosity.
descriptions.empathy: To try to understand what somebody else is feeling.
descriptions.compassion: To notice difficulty and want to ease it.
descriptions.generosity: To share time, knowledge, attention or means.
descriptions.helping: To be there when somebody needs it.
descriptions.contribution: To use what I have to create value for others.
descriptions.community: To build connection and responsibility where I live.
descriptions.equality: To treat people as equal in worth and in right.
descriptions.justice: To act for fairness and against wrong.
descriptions.environment: To act out of responsibility to the natural world.
descriptions.honesty: To say what is true and speak directly.
descriptions.integrity: To keep my values, my words and my actions in line.
descriptions.fairness: To decide without giving myself an unearned advantage.
descriptions.reliability: To be somebody whose word can be counted on.
descriptions.humility: To know what I can do without pretending to know the rest.
descriptions.meaning: To feel that my life and what I do matter.
descriptions.purpose: To serve something larger than my immediate interest.
descriptions.spirituality: To tend a connection to a deeper or wider dimension.
descriptions.gratitude: To notice what is good and value what is there.
descriptions.presence: To be here, attentive to what is happening now.

intro.lead: Which values do you want to live by, now?
intro.body: You sort cards, one at a time, and narrow down to five in your own order. Nothing is scored and nothing is shared.
intro.quickNote: Faster, and less precise. You can go deeper afterwards without starting again.
intro.resume: Pick up where you left off

sort.title: What matters most?
sort.subtitle: Sort each value by what feels true now
sort.reviewable: You can review every choice later.
sort.ownMeaning: What does it mean to you?

reduce.title: If you could keep only {{count}} for the season ahead, which would you not give up?

rank.title: Put them in order, for now.
rank.subtitle: Values reorder with a season. This is today's order, not who you are.

presence.title: How present is {{value}} in your life today?

result.title: Five values you want to live by now.
result.topLead: How closely are you living these today?
result.gap: {{value}} is the one furthest from how you are living. That distance is the useful part of this, not a failure.
result.noGap: You are living close to what you said matters. That is worth noticing.
result.talk: Talk to your coach about this
result.deepen: Want to sharpen this? You can go on to the full clarification without starting again.
result.private: Private unless you choose to share it.
result.yourSteps: The steps you named for yourself

define.title: {{value}}
define.livedLike: What does it look like when you are living by it?
define.absentLike: What makes you feel you are not?
define.step: One small step this week that would express it
define.lead: Five short questions, and every one of them is optional.

date.title: When are you writing from?
date.body: You are going to write from that day, looking back, as though the year went as well as it realistically could. Not a fantasy, and not a plan.

prepare.title: Before you start.
prepare.body: Write in the past tense, as though it has already happened. Write to somebody who has not seen you this year. And keep it realistic — the point is a year you could actually have, because that is the only kind you can walk towards.

write.title: A year has passed, and things went as well as they realistically could.
write.body: Write to someone who has not seen you this year. What changed in your everyday life?

hints.personal: What is different about how you look after yourself?
hints.work: What did you get good at, and what did you stop doing?
hints.relationships: Who did you get closer to, and how?
hints.ordinaryDay: Walk through a Tuesday. What does it actually look like?

write.dictate: Use the microphone on your keyboard to speak instead of typing.

deliver.title: When should this come back to you?
deliver.body: It stays on this phone. Nothing is sent anywhere.
deliver.checkpoint: Also check in after six months
deliver.checkpointNote: Not a reminder to do anything. A chance to ask whether you still mean it, and whether you are moving that way.

result.title: It is written.
result.returns: It comes back to you on {{date}}.
result.checkpointOn: You will hear from it once before then, on {{date}}.
result.dreamsLead: Anything in there you are actually aiming at? Keep it as a Dream. You choose, and you can edit it.
result.dreamPlaceholder: Name what you are aiming at

readBack.letter: You wrote this a while ago, for today.
readBack.checkpoint: Halfway. You wrote this on {{date}} — is it still what you want, and are you moving that way?

direction.title: Direction Statement
direction.notADream: This is a direction, not a commitment or a Dream.

intro.lead: One sentence about where you are pointed.
intro.body: It brings together what draws you and what you naturally bring. It is not a goal and nothing gets planned from it — it is a long-term reading that helps the coach phrase Dreams later, in your language rather than ours.

draws.title: What draws you?
draws.body: Pick up to three. These came from the values you already narrowed down; add anything that is missing.
draws.empty: Nothing here yet — write what pulls you.

brings.title: And what do you naturally bring?
brings.body: Pick up to three. Nobody has told us this yet, so it is yours to write. Not what you should be good at — what people actually come to you for.

drafts.title: Five ways of saying it.
drafts.body: Same words, different weight. Pick the one that sounds like you.
drafts.label: Draft {{n}}

templates.leadWithPull: I want to {{draw}} by using my {{a}}{{andB}}.
templates.leadWithPerson: I am at my best when my {{a}} helps somebody {{draw}}.
templates.leadWithPractice: I keep practising {{a}} so that I can {{draw}}.

refine.title: Bring together what draws you and what you naturally bring.

trim.title: Now make it yours.
trim.body: Edit it freely. Around eight to twelve words tends to be sayable, but it is your sentence.

gloss.title: What do these words mean to you?
gloss.body: Every one of them means something different to different people. This is optional, and it is the part a coach will actually read.

result.title: Your direction, for now.
result.note: Nothing is planned from this. When you are ready to work on something, the coach can start here.

intro.lead: Let's notice what brings you alive.
intro.body: Six short prompts, and up to eight Sparks — moments, activities and subjects that draw you in. There are no right answers, and this is only a starting map. You can test it against real life later.
intro.editable: Your map stays yours to edit.

prompts.energy: What can you do for a long time and still feel more energized afterward?
prompts.naturalReturn: What do you keep coming back to, even when nobody asks?
prompts.absorption: When did you recently lose track of time, in a good way?
prompts.contribution: What do people ask you for help with that you genuinely enjoy?
prompts.noJudgment: If you knew nobody would judge you, what would you try, learn or make?
prompts.meaningfulChange: What change, in your life or someone else's, would feel worth contributing to?

collect.capReached: That is eight. Review them before adding another.

review.title: Which three to five feel strongest today?
review.body: Everything you collected is here. Edit or remove anything, then choose the ones that ring truest right now.
review.earlyClues: Fewer than four is fine — the result will be early clues rather than a map, and nothing will be invented to fill it.

why.title: What is it about this that draws you in?

arrange.title: Shape your map
arrange.body: These groupings are suggestions. Rename them, move a Spark, or leave one on its own.

result.title: Your passion map
result.clues: These are clues, not labels. Your map can change as you learn from real life.
result.noInsightYet: Add signals from real moments and patterns will appear here.
result.feedsNextRun: {{count}} moments recorded since. They shape the result the next time you run this.

signal.title: What stood out today?
signal.body: A quick signal, to keep your map up to date.
signal.what: What was the moment or activity?
signal.placeholder: e.g. helped a friend with their CV
signal.full: Three moments is plenty for one day.

proposal.strengthen: {{subject}} has energized you across {{days}} different days. Worth adding to your map?
proposal.question: {{subject}} has drained you across {{days}} different days. Worth a second look at what it means?

mode.title: How would you like to receive feedback?
mode.body: Both help you grow. They are different promises to the people you ask, so choose before you invite anybody.
mode.visibleBody: Invite one or more people. You see each response with their name.
mode.confidentialBody: Invite at least five. You receive one de-identified summary per question, and never the raw responses.
mode.howBody: We hide identities and remove identifying details before writing the summary. We say de-identified rather than anonymous, because context can still make somebody guessable — and saying otherwise would be a promise we cannot keep.
mode.locked: Once you invite the first person, the mode and the questions are fixed. Changing either starts a new round.

pick.title: What would you like to learn?

custom.title: Write your own question
custom.placeholder: What helps me bring out the best in a team?
custom.readyBody: Our review found no identifying or sensitive details.
custom.guidance: Avoid names, diagnoses, intimate details, or anything that could identify who answered.

problems.multipleQuestions: This looks like two questions. People answer the first one and the second quietly disappears.
problems.namesSomeone: This names somebody. That is usually a slip, and in a confidential round it can identify a person.
problems.asksForJudgement: This asks people to judge you rather than tell you what they saw. That is a different tool, and a harder one to hear.
problems.sensitive: This asks about something too personal to put in front of a friend.

bank.atMyBest: When have you seen me at my best?
bank.handledDifficulty: When have you seen me handle something difficult well?
bank.leftImpression: What action of mine left an impression on you?
bank.helpedSomeone: When have you seen me help somebody in a way that mattered?
bank.mostNatural: In what situations do I seem most myself?
bank.strengthStandsOut: Which of my strengths stands out most to you?
bank.qualityTrust: What makes it easier for you to trust me?
bank.peopleAskFor: What do people naturally ask me for help with?
bank.underestimate: What am I good at that I probably underestimate?
bank.bringToGroup: What do I bring to a group that others often do not?
bank.positiveImpact: What effect do I have on the people around me?
bank.howIMakePeopleFeel: How do people feel around me when I am at my best?
bank.whatPeopleGain: What do people get from having me in their lives?
bank.useMoreOften: Which of my strengths should I use more often?
bank.smallChange: What small change would help me be more like that?

review.title: Review and send
review.whoTitle: Who would you like to ask?
review.noFriends: Nobody is in your Support Circle yet. Mirror asks people who already know you, so this is where it starts.
review.visibleAnyNumber: Even one person is enough for a visible round.
review.needMore: A confidential round needs at least {{count}} people, so that no single answer can be recognised.
review.failed: That did not go out. Nothing was sent, and nothing was lost — try again.
review.offline: This needs a connection. Nothing was sent.

round.collectingNote: The round is open for a week. The result opens when it closes, never as answers arrive — so nobody can work out when you were answered.
round.nudge: Not enough people have answered yet. Adding a few more is the thing that helps, and everyone gets at least five days from the moment you do.
round.notEnough: Not enough people answered, so there is no summary to show.
round.notEnoughBody: That is not a failure of yours. Confidential feedback needs five answers to every question before it can be shown safely, and the responses that did come in have been deleted.
round.sealed: Results open only after the confidentiality threshold is met.
round.neverRaw: Raw responses are never shown to you.
round.noPattern: No shared pattern was strong enough to show safely.
round.unavailable: We could not put the result together just now.
round.leakedNote: This one came too close to somebody’s own wording, so it is not shown.
round.emptyNote: Nothing usable came back for this question.

sent.title: The invitations are out
sent.visible: {{count}} people were asked. Their answers appear here as they arrive, with their names on them, and the round closes in {{days}} days.
sent.confidential: {{count}} people were asked. Nothing will be shown until enough of them have answered — and then it comes back as a pattern, never as somebody's words. The round closes in {{days}} days.

answer.title: Somebody asked what you see

mode.visible: They will read your answers, with your name
mode.visibleBody: Write what you would say to them directly. They see your words as you wrote them.
mode.confidential: Nobody will ever see what you wrote
mode.confidentialBody: Not even the person who asked. Your answer joins several others and only a shared pattern comes back — so you can be completely honest.

answer.privateReading: Reading this is private. They are not told that you opened it, and only sending changes anything.
answer.placeholder: Only if you have something to say…
answer.none: Nothing is waiting for you right now.
answer.failed: That did not go through. Nothing was sent.
answer.thanksBody: What you wrote is on its way, exactly as the promise above said it would be.

intro.lead: The good things get lost in the day quickly. Writing them down is what keeps them for a while longer.
intro.outcome: A private record of at least five people, moments or ordinary things you appreciated.

daily.title: Daily record
daily.blurb: Five small or large things from today.

weekly.title: Weekly record
weekly.blurb: A wider look at the people and moments of the week.

entries.promptDaily: What can you thank today for?
entries.promptWeekly: What can you thank this week for?
entries.help: A person, a moment, something that worked out. Small counts.
entries.draftSaved: Saved as you write. You can leave and come back.

prompts.title: If nothing comes to mind
prompts.smallMoments: A small moment that passed quietly
prompts.body: Something your body carried you through
prompts.places: A place you felt good in
prompts.takenForGranted: Something you usually take for granted

deepen.prompt: Want to look at one of them more closely?
deepen.help: Optional. A full list is a full record on its own.

why.prompt: Why is this moment precious to you?
why.help: A short sentence is enough. A long one is fine too.

result.title: {{count}} things worth remembering
result.private: This record stays on your phone. Nobody reads it, and nothing in the app learns from it.

whatWorked.title: What worked for me

intro.lead: Progress is rarely a straight line, and the moments it does move are worth looking at closely. Something worked. It is worth knowing what stood behind it.
intro.outcome: A short record of one thing that worked and what may have helped it.

day.title: Look at today
day.blurb: One fresh moment, while it is still clear.

week.title: Look at the week
week.blurb: Find what repeated across several days.

moment.questionDay: Where did something work well today?
moment.questionWeek: Where did something work well this week?
moment.help: It does not have to be big. Something small you managed on a heavy day counts.
moment.label: Moment number {{index}}

conditions.question: What helped it happen?
conditions.help: Choose what fits. More than one is fine, and so is none.

options.planning: I had planned it in advance

contribution.question: What was your part in it?
contribution.help: Only if there was one. Some things work out because of luck or because of somebody else, and that is a true answer too.

idea.question: What is worth trying again?
idea.help: One small thing you could repeat. Not a plan, and not a promise.

whatWorked.autosave: Saved as you write. You can leave and come back.

result.title: It has worked once already
result.private: This record stays on your phone. It is evidence for you, not a score, and nothing in the app reads it.

intro.lead: When it is hard, it is worth turning toward yourself the way you would turn toward someone you love. Not to fix anything. Just to stop being alone with it for a minute.
intro.outcome: A short pause, and one kind sentence to take with you.

read.title: Read at my own pace
read.blurb: You move between the sentences yourself.

audio.title: Short audio guidance
audio.blurb: A recorded voice takes you through it, hands free.
audio.note: The recording is not ready yet. The reading path is complete.

acknowledge.help: You can say that sentence without being at war with yourself over it.

humanity.line: You are not alone in this.
humanity.help: Difficulty, doubt and failure are part of being human. They are not proof that something is wrong with you.

kindness.question: What would you say to someone you love?
kindness.help: Choose a sentence that feels honest to you, or write your own.
kindness.customLabel: A sentence in my own words
kindness.optional: You can also carry on without a sentence.

phrases.allowedHuman: I am allowed to be human
phrases.bestYouCould: I did the best I could with what I had
phrases.allowedHard: It is allowed to be hard right now

finish.title: This moment belongs only to you
finish.noPhrase: No sentence, and that is complete too.
finish.nothingSaved: Nothing was saved. Nobody knows you were here.

decisionClarity.title: What really matters to me

intro.lead: Being torn is not weakness. It usually means both sides hold something real, and it is easier to see them when they are not shouting at once.
intro.outcome: The four sides of one decision, and a sentence of your own about what became clearer.

topic.question: What change are you considering?
topic.help: One question, in your own words. There is no right answer here, and this tool will not choose for you.

topicChanged.title: The question changed
topicChanged.body: What you already wrote was about the earlier question. Do you want to keep it, or start this decision fresh?

statusQuoBenefits.question: What does the current situation give you?
statusQuoBenefits.help: Even a situation you want to leave is meeting some real need. Naming it is not an argument for staying.

statusQuoCosts.question: What does the current situation cost you?
statusQuoCosts.help: What you pay for it, in time, energy or something else.

changeBenefits.question: What might change give you?
changeBenefits.help: Possibilities, not promises. Nobody can guarantee them, including this tool.

changeCosts.question: What might change cost you, or make hard?
changeCosts.help: A worry named out loud is not a prediction that it will happen.

priorities.question: Which of these weighs most on you?
priorities.help: Choose up to {{max}}, in your own order. Nothing here is counted or scored.
priorities.nothingWritten: Nothing was written on the four sides, and that is fine. You can carry on.

clarity.question: What became clearer?
clarity.help: Not what you decided. Just what you can see now that you could not see before.
clarity.placeholder: What is clearer to me is…

decisionClarity.emptyHint: Nothing yet. You can also carry on without writing anything here.
decisionClarity.nothingComesToMind: Nothing comes to mind right now
decisionClarity.noRightAnswer: There is no right answer, and this tool will not decide for you.

result.private: This reflection stays on your phone. There is no score here and no recommendation, because the decision is yours.

currentLoad.title: What am I carrying right now

intro.lead: Overload is usually a feeling before it is a fact. One finished week, divided the way it really went, turns the feeling into something you can look at.
intro.outcome: A map of one week: where your time went, what gave and took energy, and what got too little room.

last.title: Last week
last.blurb: Good when it roughly resembles your life now.

choose.title: Choose another week
choose.blurb: Good when last week was unusual.

week.question: Which week should we look at?
week.help: Only finished weeks. The week you are living now is hard to describe from inside it.
week.representative: Does this week resemble your life at the moment?

allocate.question: How was your week divided?
allocate.help: A hundred tiles for the whole week. Choose an area and give it as much room as it took.
allocate.noHours: No need for exact hours. A rough sense is the point.
allocate.gridLabel: A hundred tiles for the week, {{used}} of {{total}} placed

energy.question: And what did each area do to your energy?
energy.help: Time and energy are two different things. A short thing can lift you and a long one can empty you.

missing.question: What got less room than you wanted?
missing.help: One area. This is what matters to you, not what should matter.

shift.question: What small shift would you want to try?
shift.help: Not a plan. One small thing, and only if you want to.

result.title: Your week map
result.mostRoom: Most of the room went to {{areas}}.
result.tooLittle: {{area}} got less room than you wanted.
result.experiment: The shift you want to try
result.private: This map stays on your phone. It describes one week, and it says nothing about who you are.

obstacle.title: From obstacle to action

intro.lead: Most plans do not fail because the goal was wrong. They fail at one predictable moment, and that moment can be prepared for.
intro.outcome: One sentence: when this happens, I will do that. In your words, and small enough to actually do.

journey.title: Something inside a Journey
journey.blurb: A difficulty that keeps coming back in a Journey you are on.

dream.title: Something from a Dream
dream.blurb: An obstacle tied to something far off you want.

standalone.title: Something else entirely
standalone.blurb: Not connected to anything in the app.

topic.help: This only sets the context. Nothing here will change what you chose.

wish.question: What would you like to happen?
wish.help: Something you can influence yourself. One thing, not a whole life.

outcome.question: What would change if it worked?
outcome.help: Optional. Sometimes it is easier to see the obstacle after you see what is on the other side.

obstacle.question: What inside you usually stops it?
obstacle.help: Not the world, and not other people. The thing in you that shows up at that moment: tiredness, avoidance, the thought that it is too big.

builder.question: So what will you do when it shows up?
builder.help: Two halves. The first is the moment you will recognise, the second is one small thing you will do.
builder.whenPlaceholder: the moment I sit down on the sofa after dinner
builder.thenPlaceholder: put my shoes by the door

flags.triggerVague: Would you recognise that moment as it happens? The more concrete it is, the better it works.
flags.responseVague: What exactly will you do? One specific action is easier to start.
flags.responseNotYours: Part of this seems to depend on someone else. What is the part that is only yours?
flags.responseSeveralActions: There is more than one action here. Which is the first one?
flags.responsePromisesTooMuch: This promises quite a lot. What is the smallest version you would still do on a bad day?

lexicon.otherPeople: they, he, she, them, my boss, my partner, someone, somebody
lexicon.guarantees: always, never, completely, forever, every single, without fail

check.title: One look before you keep it
check.help: These are questions, not corrections. You can keep exactly what you wrote.
check.clearTitle: That reads like something you could do
check.clearHelp: The moment is recognisable and the action is yours. Keep it.
check.refineFailed: Nothing better came back. What you wrote stands.

obstacle.autosave: Saved as you write. You can leave and come back.

result.title: Your response, ready for the moment

supportMap.title: My support map

intro.lead: Nobody is one person's whole support. The one who listens well is rarely the one who tells you the truth, and neither is the one you call with good news.
intro.outcome: A private map of the people you would want beside you, and the moments nobody comes to mind for yet.

listening.question: You had a hard day. Who would you want to listen, without rushing to fix it?
listening.help: Someone who can sit with it without turning it into a task.
listening.label: When you need to be heard

persistence.question: You are about to give up. Who could remind you why you started, without judging?
persistence.help: Not the one who pushes. The one who remembers.
persistence.label: When you are about to give up

advice.question: You need to see the next step. Whose experience would help?
advice.help: Someone who has been somewhere similar.
advice.label: When you need a next step

celebration.question: Something good happened. Who would you want to tell first?
celebration.help: The one whose happiness for you is real.
celebration.label: When something good happens

accountability.question: You want to keep your word. Who could check in gently?
accountability.help: Gently is the word. Not someone who would make you feel watched.
accountability.label: When you want to keep your word

result.title: The people around you
result.gapsNote: An empty moment is worth knowing about. It is not a failing, and it is not a reason to go looking for strangers.
result.private: This map stays on your phone. Nobody knows they are on it, nobody was contacted, and nothing about your Support Circle changed.

invite.question: Would you want any of them here?
invite.help: An invitation is an invitation to join PushApp. It is not a friend request, and it never shows anyone how you mapped them.
invite.nobody: Everyone on your map is already here.
invite.notYet: Sending an invitation is not built yet, so nothing can be sent from here. The map itself is complete and yours.
